themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 3 THIS WEEK versus 0.2 per week average over the prior 8 weeks—a 1100% increase (z-score: 6.35)—suggesting a coordinated or sudden campaign affecting neighborhood visibility and property values.
evidence: 3 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Z-score of 6.35 indicates statistically extreme spike
1100% increase represents most dramatic single-category surge in district data
reporting_angles: Ground survey of Fort Greene and Brooklyn Heights to document what's being posted (political, commercial, other) and where clusters appear
Interview DOE Sanitation about response capacity and whether this reflects contractor gaps or organized posting campaigns

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints jumped to 61 THIS WEEK from 21.5 weekly average (184% spike, z-score: 4.55), while dangling street signs spiked 471% (5 complaints this week vs. 0.9 avg), signaling accelerating pavement and signage failures across the district.
evidence: Street condition complaints: 61 this week vs. 21.5 weekly average—184% spike
Dangling street signs: 5 this week vs. 0.9 weekly average—471% spike (z-score: 5.28)
Combined signal suggests systemic infrastructure maintenance failure, not isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Walk-and-document audit of major streets (Washington Park, Atlantic Avenue, Flatbush) to photograph pothole patterns, sign damage, and sidewalk hazards
DOT inspection records and repaving schedules for CD 302; ask why response lags spikes in complaints

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk & Graffiti Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints surged to 20 LAST WEEK from 7.6 weekly average (162% increase, z-score: 4.96), and graffiti complaints rose to 11 (184% spike, z-score: 4.64), indicating simultaneous physical decay and vandalism pressure in high-foot-traffic areas.
evidence: Sidewalk condition complaints: 20 last week vs. 7.6 weekly average—162% spike (z-score: 4.96)
Graffiti complaints: 11 last week vs. 3.9 weekly average—184% spike (z-score: 4.64)
Two-indicator convergence suggests organized decay or deferred maintenance across public realm
reporting_angles: Interview residents and businesses on Myrtle Avenue, Fort Greene Park perimeter, and Brooklyn Heights Promenade about visibility and use patterns
Request Parks Department and DOT maintenance schedules; ask whether staffing or budget cuts correlate with spike timeline

themes_detail.label: Sewer System Stress
themes_detail.summary: Sewer complaints peaked at 19 TWO WEEKS AGO versus 4.0 weekly average—a 375% spike (z-score: 6.26)—potentially signaling blockages, overflow risk, or infrastructure failure ahead of heavier use or weather.
evidence: Sewer complaints: 19 two weeks ago vs. 4.0 weekly average—375% spike (z-score: 6.26)
High z-score indicates severe anomaly; timing suggests ongoing condition rather than one-off event
Proximity to heat/hot water complaints (1,674 over 90 days) suggests possible water-system interconnection issues
reporting_angles: File DEP records request for sewer complaints, service requests, and inspections in CD 302 over past month; ask about blockages and overflow events
Interview residents reporting sewer odors or backups; map complaint locations to identify hotspots

themes_detail.label: Street-Level Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 63 LAST WEEK from 16.6 weekly average (279% increase, z-score: 5.15), while vehicle noise rose 130% two weeks ago (23 vs. 10.0 avg), indicating construction, delivery, or traffic changes disrupting outdoor spaces.
evidence: Street/sidewalk noise: 63 last week vs. 16.6 weekly average—279% spike (z-score: 5.15)
Vehicle noise: 23 two weeks ago vs. 10.0 weekly average—130% spike (z-score: 4.6)
Dual-source noise spike suggests specific disruptive event (construction, delivery restrictions lift, transit change) rather than baseline increase
reporting_angles: Cross-check against DOB construction permits issued in past 3 weeks; identify active projects on Myrtle, Atlantic, Flatbush, and Washington Avenue
Interview Fort Greene Park and Brooklyn Heights Promenade users about when noise increased; ask whether new delivery windows or shuttle services began
